title: Admin Safe‑Mode Procedures and Support Macros for RBACv2
creator: Lina Morales
description:
Purpose: Condensed, actionable safe‑mode & triage guide for oncall/support to safely recover and mitigate RBACv2 misconfigurations, plus ready‑to‑paste support macros for SSO/SAML validation and audit queries. This ticket produces: (1) a one‑page Safe‑Mode checklist for frontline responders, (2) a short escalation script for delegated admins, (3) a set of audit query templates and recommended dashboards to check privileges and recent admin activity, and (4) support macros (Slack/Helpdesk) for common recovery flows.

Scope: Hosted control plane and Dedicated admin console flows. Does not include private on‑prem installer steps (separate runbook). Covers: admin lockout, bad role bindings, stale service principals, failed SSO assertions, unusual audit spikes, emergency temporary elevation, and cleanup/forensics notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- One‑page printable Safe‑Mode checklist with exact CLI/API commands and timeouts.
- 5 support macros covering: Admin lockout recovery, SAML identity check, temporary elevation + audit capture, revoke-compromised-keys, and post‑incident cleanup.
- Audit query templates (SQL/ES/Kibana) that return actionable rows (user, action, target, raw_assertion_id, timestamp).
- Signoff from Security SME (Anika Rao) and Support manager (Jordan Lee).

runbook_steps: Step 0 — Situation assessment (first 5 minutes): Confirm symmetric symptoms across tenants (UI 403 vs API 403), check control plane health dashboard, and whether SSO provider reports errors.
Step 1 — Enter Safe‑Mode: Initiate 'console read-only' gating to block new role mutations: POST /internal/admin/gate?safe_mode=true (15s TTL). Notify stakeholders in incident channel.
Step 2 — Snapshot audit trail: Export last 6 hours of rbac-audit-* to S3 path: s3://redwood-rbac-forensics/eng-<ticket>-<date>. Use retention tag 'forensics-72h'.

Step 3 — Identify likely cause: Run 'Recent Admin Grants' query (see audit_queries). If >3 distinct IPs or unexpected OAuth client IDs present, mark as potential compromise and escalate to SecOps immediately.

Step 4 — Temporary mitigation (least privilege): Create a scoped emergency role 'temp_recovery_<ts>' with minimal perms to correct bindings; set auto-revoke at +30m (use /api/v2/roles?expires_at=...). Do not grant 'iam:owner' scope.
Step 5 — Execute corrective action: Revoke only implicated role bindings or service principals; prefer role patch over role delete. Record change and include PR/changeset link in incident timeline.

Step 6 — SAML validation flow (if SSO suspected): a) Pull assertion_id from audit row, b) POST assertion_id to /internal/identity/validate-assertion, c) log IdP response and relay to IdP contact. If assertion signature fails, instruct IdP to rotate signing cert and rotate affected sessions.
Step 7 — Reopen write access: After verification and a 30m stabilization window, remove safe_mode gate and observe metrics for 60 minutes. If anomalies recur, reenter safe mode and escalate.

Step 8 — Post‑mortem checklist: Attach exported audit snapshot, list of changed bindings, temporary roles created, KMS key checks (if keys rotated), and follow‑ups: policy hardening, runbook updates, and scheduled runbook drill.
support_macros:
Macro: ADMIN_LOCKOUT_RECOVERY
Title: Admin console lockout – recovery steps
Text: Hi <@user>, we're investigating an admin console access issue. First, confirm if you see 403 or SSO error. If 403, request a scoped temporary role for you: /api/internal/request-temp?user=<email>&reason=<short_reason>&ttl=30m. If SSO error, include the IdP 'error_id' from the console and run 'check_saml_assertion' macro. We'll escalate to SecOps if we detect multiple anomalous IPs.

Macro: CHECK_SAML_ASSERTION
Title: Validate SAML assertion with IdP
Text: Run: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $BOT_TOKEN' -d '{"assertion_id": "<assertion_id>"}' https://console.internal/api/internal/identity/validate-assertion. Paste response. If "signature_valid":false then escalate to IdP owner and flag for cert rotation.

Macro: TEMP_ELEVATION_WITH_AUDIT
Title: Issue temporary elevation and capture audit snapshot
Text: Steps:
1) Create role: POST /api/v2/roles {name: 'temp_recovery_<ts>', perms: ['rbac:modify_bindings'], expires_at: <iso> }
2) Record role_id and user in incident timeline.
3) Run audit export: /internal/audit/export?from=-60m&to=now&path=s3://...
4) Auto-revoke timer scheduled (30m).
Note: Never grant wildcard owner scope.

Macro: REVOKE_COMPROMISED_CLIENT
Title: Revoke a compromised OAuth client or service principal
Text: Steps:
1) Mark client as 'disabled' in Admin UI.
2) Revoke tokens: POST /api/oauth/revoke?client_id=<id>.
3) Audit: Run 'service_principal_actions' query and attach rows.
4) Rotate client secret and schedule a coordinated rollout with integrators.

Macro: POST_INCIDENT_CLEANUP
Title: Post-incident hygiene checklist
Text: Checklist: export audit, rotate temporary creds, confirm KMS key integrity, create follow-up tickets for policy hardening, schedule a runbook drill, update this runbook with any new edge-cases observed.
audit_queries: Recent_Admin_Grants (ES/Kibana): {"index":"rbac-audit-*","query":{"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"action":"role.bind"}},{"range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"now-6h"}}}]}}} -- returns user, role_id, target, ip, raw_assertion_id, request_id
Failed_SAML_Assertions: SELECT timestamp, user_email, raw_assertion_id, error_code FROM rbac_audit WHERE action='sso.assertion' AND result='failure' AND timestamp > now()-interval '24 hours';
Service_Principal_Actions: {index:'rbac-audit-*', q:'target.type:service_principal AND @timestamp:[now-24h TO now]'} -- use to enumerate recent secret rotations, token issues, or unexpected grants

Privileged_Action_History: SELECT timestamp, user, action, resource, request_id FROM actions WHERE action IN ('role.create','role.update','role.bind','role.unbind') AND timestamp > now()-interval '7 days' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 250;
